purpose: Sotorasib is used to treat a certain type of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in adults. It is specifically for cancers that have a gene mutation called KRAS G12C. Your doctor will test your tumor to make sure this medication is the right fit for you.
how_it_works: Inside cancer cells, there is a faulty protein caused by the KRAS G12C mutation that tells the cancer to keep growing out of control. Sotorasib works like a lock-and-key — it attaches directly to that faulty protein and blocks it from sending those 'keep growing' signals. By shutting off this signal, the drug helps slow down or stop the cancer from spreading.
common_side_effects: Diarrhea, nausea, stomach pain, tiredness, joint or muscle pain, cough, constipation, and decreased appetite are the most commonly reported side effects. Some patients also notice changes in liver blood tests, so your doctor will check your labs regularly.
warnings: This medication can cause serious liver problems — tell your doctor right away if you notice yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or unusual tiredness. It can also cause lung inflammation (called pneumonitis), which may feel like new or worsening shortness of breath or cough. Avoid taking antacids at the same time as this medication, as they can reduce how well it works. This drug may harm an unborn baby, so effective birth control is very important during treatment.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 960 mg (eight 120 mg tablets) taken by mouth once a day. It can be taken with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day, and swallow the tablets whole — do not crush or chew them. If you miss a dose and it has been more than 6 hours, skip it and take the next dose as scheduled.
